rationale: Joint replacement of both observed MeanSAGE module forwards (encoder.first = 206dbc4bff7ae767415599c9, group f2cad7658bd2e042c326; encoder.second = 866013201077b272e7156dd4, group b63063a25115d472ba96) with a CSR segment-sum Triton composite implementing the selected hypothesis. Measured basis (selection.json, target-resources.json, nsys-9ed9145c): the per-layer chain index_select -> zeros_like -> index_add_ -> clamp_min -> unsqueeze -> div -> cat costs 259.8 us of the 321.8 us diagnostic CUDA total; layer 1 gathers a 32 MB messages tensor (vectorized_gather_kernel 34.98 us) then re-reads it in indexFuncLargeIndex ReduceAdd (45.95 us), layer 2 repeats with 64 MB (54.05 us + 98.63 us); both GEMMs (36.99/21.50 us) are near their fp32 compute floor and are left untouched. The replacement, executed inside the replacement on every invocation, rebuilds per layer: one int32 zero-fill (3*4096) + one Triton histogram of destinations (65,536 relaxed int32 atomics), one torch.cumsum(int32) inclusive scan into the same buffer, one Triton scatter that stably ranks edges per destination (65,536 relaxed int32 atomics) producing a destination-sorted int32 source array, then one Triton segsum kernel whose programs accumulate source rows in registers per (node, 128-column) segment and write buf[:, :F] = features and buf[:, F:] = acc / max(degree, 1) directly into the [features | neighbors] projection input (the features copy replaces aten::cat's read of a separate neighbors tensor). The original fp32 semantics are preserved pointwise: every directed edge (including duplicates) contributes individually because the histogram counts every edge; nodes without incoming edges get cnt = 0, acc = 0, denominator max(0, 1) = 1, i.e. zero neighbor features exactly as zeros_like/index_add_/clamp_min(1); the division lowers to div.rn.f32 (verified in generated PTX), the same IEEE correctly-rounded fp32 division aten::div uses, not a reciprocal multiply; column order [features | neighbors] matches aten::cat dim=1; the project module is invoked normally (module.project(buf)) so the Linear module boundaries (a1535028e5ecfcb604215494, e9cbf5739bc84264b863c3fe) and their aten::linear functional sites (3917cd1f557688d0fef2351c, 12be5e599f9b66632f879389) execute with exactly the observed [4096, 512]/[4096, 256] fp32 contiguous signatures, and the returned tensor is the same fresh Linear output with no aliasing of inputs. Remaining numeric difference vs the reference is the summation order of the ~16 fp32 terms per (node, column): the reference's index_add_ reduces in nondeterministic atomic order while this implementation reduces in CSR order; both are correct fp32 summations whose divergence is ~1e-7 relative, far inside atol 1e-5 / rtol 1e-4 (the original harness already compares two atomic-order runs under these tolerances). Expected effect (hypothesis, to be measured by the framework): the 96 MB messages write+read round trip and the 8.4M/16.8M fp32 L2 atomic adds are replaced by ~25 M request-local int32 atomics and coalesced row reads (features working set 2/4 MB is L2-resident), cutting per-layer aggregation cost from 91.1/168.7 us toward roughly 35-60 us and reducing median latency_ms from the 0.373 ms baseline toward ~0.20-0.25 ms; per-layer kernel count drops from 7 to 6 (zero-fill+histogram, cumsum, scatter, segsum, GEMM) and the 32/64 MB messages intermediates disappear from the allocator. Dispatch-only tricks (CUDA Graph capture) were deliberately not used: the binding contract notes replay does not rerun Python hooks and cannot prove inherited native execution, while this path executes real kernels through the normal stream on every invocation. The four profiler record_function sites (5e90f195f7f306db14a8148e, dfe44b1cfe55fcdce017af05, ef8be01433c0dd9f87d7d2b9, f6b685d75a61f7577e0e2b09) are 0.0 us instrumentation ranges around the module boundaries, not computational work; they are emitted by the framework's boundary machinery rather than model.py and are neither claimed as eliminated nor relied upon. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt exists, so there is no prior feedback to incorporate; this is the first candidate on this selection. Route labels are self-reported via context['record_route'] inside the replacement: 'triton_csr_segsum' on the fused path, 'fallback:signature' for non-matching signatures, 'fallback:runtime' for a caught runtime failure, 'fallback:setup' when Triton or the project attribute is unavailable at build; every fallback calls the parent bound forward from context['references'], so quality and coverage degrade to parent behavior rather than failing.

setup_work.build_time: No GPU work, no model mutation, no weight packing and no fixture-dependent precomputation at build(): the module only defines the three Triton JIT functions and returns bound closures over context['modules'][call_id].project and context['references'][call_id]. The workload executes fully on every invocation.
setup_work.first_invocation: Triton JIT compilation of the three kernels (hist and scatter once, segsum specialized for F=128 and F=256) happens on the first forward that takes the fused path; the frozen harness performs 3 warmup invocations before the 15 timed samples, so compilation and cubin caching land in warmup. This cost appears in lifecycle counters (framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include preparation and the compilation allocations) but not in the per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes of warm repeats.
setup_work.per_invocation: Each layer forward rebuilds the derived CSR structure from the live destinations tensor: one torch.zeros(3*4096, int32) (48 KB), one histogram kernel, one torch.cumsum into a view of the same buffer, one scatter kernel producing a 65,536-entry int32 sorted-source array (256 KB), then the segsum kernel writing a [4096, 2F] fp32 buffer (4 MB layer 1, 8 MB layer 2) that feeds project. Nothing persists across invocations (adapter reset is a no-op and every buffer is freshly allocated inside the forward), satisfying the no-cross-invocation-state constraint.
setup_work.memory: Warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes is expected to fall substantially because the messages intermediates (32 MB layer 1, 64 MB layer 2) are no longer materialized; that is a per-run PyTorch allocator counter decrease, not a general physical-memory saving, and no non-PyTorch driver memory is measured. No CUDA Graphs are captured, so no graph pools are retained and reserved memory does not grow on that account.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Inference-only under torch.inference_mode(); no parameters, buffers or optimizer state are modified, no gradients exist, and inputs are never written (all kernel writes target freshly allocated buffers).

quality_risks: Summation-order divergence from the reference: the reference reduces each node's messages in nondeterministic atomic order (index_add_) while this implementation reduces in CSR order. Bounded by fp32 summation error of ~16-45 terms (~1e-7 relative), orders of magnitude inside atol 1e-5 / rtol 1e-4; verified exactly equal to the reference formula in a CPU emulation of the kernel math on seeded fixtures.
Division rounding: segsum uses tl.math.div_rn, confirmed to emit div.rn.f32 (IEEE correctly rounded), matching aten::div on fp32; using x * (1/den) was deliberately avoided.

Index bounds are trusted as in-bounds (0 <= sources[i], destinations[i] < N): the frozen fixture generates them with randint(N), and the signature guard restricts the fused path to int64 1-D contiguous CUDA index tensors. Out-of-range indices would corrupt memory instead of raising like index_select; this is accepted for the frozen workload and mitigated by the fallback guard for any other shape/dtype/stride combination.

Any signature deviation (dtype, dims, strides, F not a multiple of 128, N > 65535 grid-y bound, CPU tensors) routes to the parent bound forward with a 'fallback:signature' label, and any runtime exception inside the fused path routes to the parent with 'fallback:runtime', so output correctness never depends on the fused path succeeding.

Triton unavailability at build time installs parent-passthrough replacements labeled 'fallback:setup' rather than failing installation; the measured worker environment ships triton 3.7.1 with torch 2.13.0+cu129.
The two GEMMs, ReLU and all encoder-level orchestration are unchanged; the aten::linear calls see byte-identical shapes/dtypes/strides to the observed signatures.
